Game Concept: STARSTRUCK: Fashion Frenzy

A multiplayer fashion runway game inspired by the social competition and styling gameplay of Dress to Impress and It Girl, but with its own identity, features, and progression.

Genre

Multiplayer Fashion 

Social Roleplay 

Runway Competition 

Dress-Up 

Life Simulation 

Target Players

Ages 9+ 

Friends 

Fashion lovers 

Casual and competitive players 

Story

You arrive in Star City, the world's biggest fashion capital. Every day, famous designers host themed fashion shows where models compete for trophies, fame, exclusive clothing, and luxury apartments.

Become the next global fashion icon by winning competitions, building your wardrobe, and collecting rare outfits.

Gameplay Loop

Join server 

Theme appears 

Shop for clothing 

Customize body, hair, makeup, accessories 

Pose on runway 

Players vote 

Winners receive rewards 

Unlock more fashion items 

Repeat

Anti-Cheat & Fair Play

Outfit plagiarism detection that highlights nearly identical submissions. 

Automatic filtering for inappropriate outfit names or chat. 

AFK detection to prevent inactive players from winning rewards. 

Vote balancing to reduce unfair group voting. 

Unique Features

Designer Studio: Create clothing using unlocked patterns, fabrics, and decals to build your own fashion collections. 

Trend Meter: Each day, featured colors, styles, or accessories give a small score bonus when used creatively. 

Fashion Magazine: Winning outfits may appear on a weekly in-game magazine cover. 

Photo Studio: Take high-quality screenshots with custom lighting, backgrounds, and poses. 

Team Runways: Compete in pairs or teams to create coordinated outfits. 

Fashion Academy: Complete tutorials and style challenges to unlock advanced customization options. 

Style Seasons: A seasonal progression system with free and premium reward tracks featuring exclusive cosmetics. 

This concept captures the appeal of runway fashion games while adding original progression, social features, creative tools, and customization systems to establish its own identity rather than copying existing games.

answers.ask: Which of the ten maps should be built first, and do they all reuse one runway layout or is each map its own?
answers.answer: Build Luxury Mall first as the core launch map. Each map should be its own themed environment, while using the same standard runway gameplay layout for a smaller, consistent first build.

answers.ask: How many players per server? Runway length and lobby capacity both depend on it.
answers.answer: Use 10 players per server, keeping the runway show manageable while everyone receives their 20-second turn. The lobby should comfortably hold those 10 players.

answers.ask: Are the apartments part of the same map or a separate instanced space?
answers.answer: Apartments should be separate instanced spaces so home decorating and friend visits do not interfere with active fashion-show rounds.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] shape — Q: Which of the ten maps should be built first, and do they all reuse one runway layout or is each map its own? A: Build Luxury Mall first as the core launch map. Each map should be its own themed environment, while using the same standard runway gameplay layout for a smaller, consistent first build.
- [author] scale — Q: How many players per server? Runway length and lobby capacity both depend on it. A: Use 10 players per server, keeping the runway show manageable while everyone receives their 20-second turn. The lobby should comfortably hold those 10 players.
- [author] shape — Q: Are the apartments part of the same map or a separate instanced space? A: Apartments should be separate instanced spaces so home decorating and friend visits do not interfere with active fashion-show rounds.

## Enriched image prompt
Create the Luxury Mall launch environment for a polished multiplayer fashion game serving 10 players. Inside the mall, arrange a spacious social lobby leading to clothing and customization preparation booths, then to one standard raised runway with a clear walk-on entrance, audience and voting floor, and a three-place winners' podium at the runway end. Add a composed photo backdrop within the mall without crowding the main circulation. Keep the layout compact enough that 10 players can move between lobby, preparation, runway, audience, and results areas without bottlenecks. Include a visible apartment-access elevator or doorway that links to separate private apartment instances. Each apartment instance is a distinct interior with a bedroom, closet, kitchen, studio, and fashion room for decorating and friend visits. Do not build the other nine themed runway maps in this first version; the mall establishes the repeatable runway arrangement they will later reuse.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Roleplay & Avatar Sim, specifically dress-up and avatar customization. Party & Casual is secondary because the lobby, timed rounds, map voting, audience voting, and results presentation organize players socially.

## Shape and preset
Use `stage-runway`, named Zone (Stage and Dressing Rooms), for the dominant Luxury Mall map: preparation booths feed one runway and audience area. The matched preset is Dress Up. The subordinate apartment instances use `interior-single` as separate private maps; they do not replace the runway's top-level shape.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` for a 10-player mall lobby connected directly to preparation and runway spaces. Use `vignette-photo` for one dedicated fashion-photo backdrop. Use the visible half of `spawn-first-reveal`, taken from Entertainment's catalogue wording, to compose arrivals toward the mall runway. Use `winner-zone`, taken from Obby & Platformer's shared row, for the visible three-place results podium. Use `teleporter-link` as an apartment elevator or doorway that visibly represents travel to separate private instances.

## Layout requirements
Place one `spawn-first-reveal` cluster with 10 non-overlapping arrival slots in the lobby, all facing the mall's preparation-to-runway axis. Place three `winner-zone` podium positions at the runway end, ordered first through third. Place the functional `teleporter-link` at the apartment-access feature and pair it with the correct private apartment instance. Voting, timers, themes, rewards, currencies, progression, quests, and anti-cheat are mechanics rather than map placements.

## Layout components
The Luxury Mall map is the dominant segment: a 10-player lobby, preparation and clothing booths, one raised runway, audience/voting floor, three-place podium, photo backdrop, and apartment-access feature connected by broad interior walkways. The separate Apartment segment is an `interior-single` private map containing a bedroom, closet, kitchen, studio, and fashion room. The other nine named themes are deferred rather than flattened into this launch map. Frame the mall so lobby, dressing route, runway, audience, and podium read in one view; frame apartment interiors separately.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the Luxury Mall's fashion presentation first, then derive its simple top-down plan. The isometric image is authoritative because the standard runway topology is straightforward and the luxury visual identity leads; apartment interiors receive their own isometric render.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium, driven by a 10-player lobby, individual preparation booths, a full runway, and audience circulation. The theme is glamorous contemporary luxury-mall fashion with polished social spaces. `P4` is required because the Luxury Mall and private apartments are separate maps linked by `teleporter-link`; no `P3` is needed because each generated map is an interior-only space rather than an exterior-to-interior crossing.
